title: Bone types, constituents and the collagen table
guide: Skeleton 10% cardiac output. Cortical 80% (diaphysis, osteon, Haversian +, PTH/thyroid, low turnover) vs trabecular 20% (epiphysis/vertebrae, trabeculae, steroids, high turnover d/t surface:mass); osteoporosis judged on trabecular bone via BMD + TBS (normal 1.432 good; low 1.124 degraded). Constituents: cells 2%, matrix 98% (organic 30–40% type I collagen + osteopontin/osteocalcin/thrombospondin/matrix GLA (warfarin-inhibited → calcification)/fibronectin/proteoglycans; inorganic 60–70% Ca/P/Mg). Collagen disorders: I OI/EDS VII; V EDS classical; II chondrodysplasia; III EDS IV; IV Alport/Goodpasture; VII epidermolysis bullosa; VIII none.

title: Bone formation hypotheses, ALP and the bone cells
guide: Amorphous Ca phosphate → hydroxyapatite. Old: osteoblast lays type I matrix, mineralised by ALP/annexin/5'-nucleotidase; new: osteoblast → osteocyte lays matrix. ALP hydrolyses mineralisation inhibitors; not ↑ in myeloma; sources bone/kidney/placenta; GGT liver-only confirms hepatic ALP. Osteoblast mesenchymal (RUNX2 → intramembranous skull/clavicle; defect cleidocranial dysplasia). Osteocyte master regulator, mechanoreceptor, estrogen kills osteoclasts; sclerostin (unloading/estrogen deficiency) inhibits WNT1 + activates osteoclasts; FGF23 most potent phosphaturic. Osteoclast macrophage origin, CA type 2 protons, Howship lacunae.

title: RANKL/OPG, calcitonin, bone cycle and turnover markers
guide: PTH/vit D ↑ RANKL on osteoblasts → RANK + M-CSF activates osteoclast; OPG inhibits RANK–RANKL. Calcitonin inhibits osteoclast + renal Ca clearance → hypocalcaemia (Rx hypercalcaemia). Cycle: activation → resorption (3 wks) → reversal → formation → mineralisation (3 months). Resorption markers TRAP/CTP/NTX; formation total & bone ALP, osteocalcin, PICP, PINP. Vit D = Group I nuclear heterodimer (type 2), VDR+RXR on VDRE.

title: Vitamin D metabolism, jejunal action and PTH basics
guide: D3 (animal/skin) vs ergocalciferol (plant); liver 25-hydroxylase → calcidiol (long t½, storage, assay form); 24-α-hydroxylase → inactive 24,25; renal PCT 1α-hydroxylase (PTH-stimulated) → calcitriol → intestinal Ca-binding protein/Ca-ATPase/ALP → ↑Ca → inhibits PTH. Drugs: phenytoin resistance, INH inhibits 25-hydroxylase, steroids/ketoconazole inhibit 1α. Nephrotic: DBP lost, vit D normal. Jejunum TRPV5/6-calbindin-NCX1-PMCA1b; VDR anti-proliferative (skin/breast/prostate). PTH 84 aa (PTHrP 139), bioactive 1-34, t½ 2-4 min (cold chain), 2nd-gen assay 50-100 pg/mL, ↑Ca ↓P.

title: Parathyroid anatomy and the PTH–vitD–FGF23 axis
guide: Endodermal, 5-7 wks: 3rd pouch → inferior (ectopic intrathyroid m/c), 4th → superior. TFs: Tbx1 → DiGeorge (22q); GATA3 → hypoPT+SNHL+renal; GCMB/SOX3 → hypoPT. Oxyntic cells (mitochondria, sestamibi). Loop: FGF23 (−)vitD (−)PTH; PTH (+)vitD (+)FGF23; vitD (−)PTH (+)FGF23; PTH via 1α-hydroxylase. FGF23: (−)Na-P 2a phosphaturic, (−)1α, (−)PTH via Klotho (CKD resistance). PTH kidney ↑Ca ↑P-excretion; vit D ↓excretion; bone PTH resorption (intermittent low dose formation); vitD 1,25 resorption / 24,25 formation. Assay: <12 deficient 50k IU/wk ×6-8 + 600-2000/day; 12-19 ≥400/day; >20 sufficient; RDA 600/800; hydroxylation impaired calcitriol 0.25-0.5 µg.

title: PTH receptors, sigmoid rule, CaSR mutations and senile osteoporosis
guide: CVS: medial calcification, atherosclerosis, HTN. GPCR cAMP/PKA; type 1 receptor also binds PTHrP (SCC head-neck/lung paraneoplastic). Sigmoid: ↑Ca activates CaSR → ↓PTH; ↓Ca (more sensitive) → ↑PTH; ionised Ca most important; P deficiency impairs release. CaSR loss → FHH; gain → Bartter type 5. Senile osteoporosis MSC → adipocyte; claudin 16 renal Ca reabsorption.
